perspective:
**Vincent Chinana’s available information:**

- Vincent is a mechanic and has a long-time friendship with Patrick Guzman from their teenage years; they share blue-collar work and have collaborated on projects before.
- At the diner, Vincent hears Patrick is considering a new construction venture to expand his business. Vincent tells Patrick he has heard it is risky and worries about financial security; he suggests reconsidering or delaying until more information is gathered. Patrick says it seems like a good opportunity, is still weighing options, appreciates Vincent’s concern, and will think it over.
- Days later, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent says he feels Patrick is not telling him everything and feels betrayed by the lack of transparency. Patrick says it is complicated, did not want to worry Vincent with details, apologizes, says he should have been more open, and agrees to explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, during their detailed discussion, Vincent learns the situation is serious. Patrick tells him he might lose a significant amount if the investment does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses; Patrick thanks him and expresses gratitude.
- A month later, at a coffee shop, Vincent has information suggesting the venture might actually turn a profit. He hears Patrick say it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him earlier and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees and says they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent is optimistic about the joint venture. He says their combined skills can make it successful, and they begin drafting a business plan, intending to outline every step carefully. Patrick agrees and says they should cover all bases.
